passages: A river begins as a small stream high in the hills. As it runs downhill, other streams join it and it grows wider. People have always built their towns beside rivers, because a river gives water to drink, fish to eat and a road for boats.
Bread is one of the oldest foods that people make. Flour is mixed with water and left to rise, and then it is baked in a hot oven. In many countries a meal does not feel complete without it.
When the sun goes down, the air becomes cooler and the sky turns dark. The first stars appear in the east. Animals that sleep during the day wake up and begin to look for food.

A library is a place where books are kept so that many people can read them. A reader borrows a book, takes it home, and brings it back a few weeks later. In this way one book can be read by hundreds of people.
Farmers watch the weather closely. Too little rain and the plants dry out; too much rain and the fields turn to mud. A good year depends on rain that comes at the right time.
The heart is a muscle about the size of a fist. It beats all day and all night, pushing blood through the body. When a person runs, the heart beats faster so that the muscles get more oxygen.

Long ago, messages were carried by people on foot or on horses, and news could take weeks to arrive. Today a message can cross the world in less than a second. The distance is the same, but the world feels smaller.

A bridge has to carry its own weight as well as the weight of everything that crosses it. Builders choose stone, steel or wood depending on how wide the gap is. The oldest bridges still in use were built more than a thousand years ago.
Children learn to speak by listening. At first they repeat single words, then they put two words together, and after a few years they can tell a whole story. Nobody has to teach them the rules.

In winter the days are short and the nights are long. Many trees lose their leaves and some animals sleep until spring. When the days grow longer again, the first flowers push through the cold ground.

A map is a picture of a place seen from above. It shows roads, rivers and towns, and it helps travellers find their way. Every map leaves most things out, because a map that showed everything would be as large as the land itself.

Salt was once so valuable that it was used as money. It keeps food from going bad, and before there were cold rooms that mattered a great deal. Today it costs very little, and we forget how important it used to be.

The ocean covers most of the surface of the earth. Near the shore the water is shallow and full of light, but far from land it is deep, cold and dark. Many of the animals that live there have never been seen by anyone.

To count a large number of things, it helps to put them into groups. Ten groups of ten make a hundred, and ten hundreds make a thousand. With this simple idea a person can write any number using only ten signs.

A good question is often worth more than a quick answer. When someone asks why the sky is blue or why ice floats, they are doing what scientists do. The answer may take years to find, and it usually leads to another question.

Markets open early in the morning. Sellers lay out fruit, vegetables and cloth, and buyers walk between the tables comparing prices. By noon the best things are gone, and by evening the square is empty again.
